description: Four UCSF riders. Four commutes. Plenty of hills, shortcuts and stories. Ever wonder what it's really like to bike to UCSF? Join Bikes! at UCSF for a lunchtime conversation with four of our featured riders — 🚲 Terri Rice, MPH — Study & Research Data Project Manager, Epidemiology & Biostatistics🚲 Maya Ezekiel, MPH, RDN — Health Promotion Specialist🚲 Jasmine Wu — Genetic Counselor Assistant, Cancer Genetics and Prevention Program🚲 Andrew Nguyen, MPH — Research Data Analyst, CLEAR LabThey'll share: 🚴 How they got hooked on biking to UCSF 🗺️ Their favorite routes and hard-earned shortcuts 💡 Lessons learned along the way ❤️ What keeps them riding ⭐ Advice they wish they'd gotten when they started Then we'll open things up for questions. Bike-curious? E-bike curious? Wondering how anyone gets up that hill? Come hang out. No Lycra required. No judgment. No requirement that you enjoy climbing hills. Just real UCSF riders, real San Francisco commutes, and maybe a little inspiration for your next trip to campus. 📅 Tuesday, September 15 🕛 12 p.m. 💻 Zoom - https://ucsf.zoom.us/meeting/register/ksWnDpUWTK-McmyOTEfclg Bikes! at UCSF — bicycle commuters and cyclists advancing health, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform

description: Established through REDS-III and continued through REDS-IV-P, the Brazil SCD cohort is a prospective, longitudinal study designed to generate real-world evidence on the health and clinical outcomes of people living with SCD in Brazil, with a particular focus on transfusion practices and their impact on patient outcomes. This seminar series will feature investigators and clinicians from the REDS Brazil collaboration presenting key findings from the cohort and ongoing work aimed at advancing our understanding of SCD and improving transfusion practices and patient care. September 15, 2026, Shannon Kelly, MD, UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland. “Overview of SCD cohort and the main findings”September 22, 2026, Mina Cintho Ozahata, PhD, University of São Paulo. “Phenotype/genotype association studies using the Brazil SCD cohort”September 29, 2026, Brian Custer, PhD, MPH, Vitalant Research Institute. “Development of the precision transfusion medicine array and its use in RBC-IMPACT”October 6, 2026, Carla Dinardo, MD, PhD, and Monike Oliveria, MSc, Fundação Pro-Sangue, São Paulo. “RHD sequencing, alloimmunization & matching studies”We hope you join this exciting series and take the opportunity to learn from our REDS Brazil collaborators and engage in discussion around the future of SCD research.

description: BCHSI Special Invited Seminar Topic: "Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Decision Making Across Modalities" Lunch Served 12:30 – 1:00 pm Seminar 1:10 – 2:00 pm Rock Hall Auditorium & by Zoom In place of the monthly BCHSI-wide Lab meeting, we will host Dr. Dvir Aran, who is currently a Visiting Scholar at UCSF - join us in welcoming him! FEATURED SPEAKER Dvir Aran, PhD, Associate Professor Faculty of Biology\Taub Faculty of Computer Science Technion -Israel Institute of Technology In this seminar, Dr. Aran will present two recent works that illustrate how artificial intelligence can democratize clinical decision-making. The first develops a deep learning model that predicts breast cancer recurrence risk directly from histopathology images, offering a scalable alternative to costly molecular assays. The second introduces a conversational, multi-agent AI system for neurological diagnosis, which achieves higher accuracy than physicians while reducing costs. Together, these studies show how AI can extend expert-level decision support to settings with limited resources, advancing both equity and efficiency in clinical care. Participants will practice searching a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools to critique the results. There will be time for questions and discussion throughout the workshop. description: Osher WISE Course: What Should I Take? Making Informed Choices About Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Wednesdays, October 7–28, 6:00-7:30 p.m. PT Approximately 1 in 5 adults uses a plant-based herbal supplement, and 1 in 2 uses a vitamin or mineral product. Many people do not tell their health care providers about the supplements they are taking. This communication gap can increase the risk of interactions with prescription medications, existing health conditions, and other treatments. As the use of dietary supplements continues to grow, it is important for people to understand how to evaluate these products, recognize their potential benefits and risks, and identify which supplements are supported by strong scientific evidence. Accessing reliable, evidence-based information can help everyone make safer, more informed decisions about their health. This four-week course will help participants learn essential tips for dietary supplement selection and evidence-based information on the effectiveness and potential risks for supplements and herbals commonly used for longevity, heart health, bone health, and other uses. This course is chaired by UCSF Clinical Pharmacy Faculty, Dr. Candy Tsourounis and Dr. Cathi Dennehy. October 7: Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Essentials: What You Need to Know October 14: Supplements for Healthy Aging: What's Popular, and Should I Take It? October 21: Longevity: Can Supplements Help You Live Longer and Healthier? October 28: Vitamins and Minerals: What Makes Sense for You Register here Our educational programming, formerly known as Osher Mini Medical School for the Public, has been reimagined as Osher WISE (Well-being and Integrative Science for Everyone). This public education program offers courses on integrative health topics that are current and compelling, providing an opportunity for community members to become active, informed participants in their own journey to health and well-being. https://osher.ucsf.edu/Osher-WISE, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform
